paths.title: Active Directory Specialist (Pilot Slice)
entry_prerequisites: Working knowledge of Windows Server administration basics

milestones.rationale: Replication is the foundation everything else in AD operations depends on.
FSMO roles build directly on understanding multi-master replication's limits.
Kerberos authentication is a daily-operations skill independent of, but informed by, the DC-management concepts above.
gMSA is a practical automation-adjacent skill that depends on basic AD object management competence.
Forest recovery is the highest-stakes, most advanced milestone and is placed last, after the learner has the replication and FSMO grounding it depends on.

paths.dependency_notes: M5 (forest recovery) assumes M1 and M2 are complete; M3 and M4 are independent of each other and of M5's prerequisites, and could be reordered relative to each other without breaking the chain.
paths.status_rationale: Every milestone resolves to real, physically-written records (verified in 16_VALIDATION), so this is not a stub - but it covers only 5 of the ~15-20 topics a genuine AD Specialist path should eventually include (e.g. DNS/DHCP integration, Group Policy, trusts, DFSR beyond SYSVOL, AD security hardening are not yet built), so it is marked PARTIALLY_POPULATED rather than CONTENT_COMPLETE.
